_doc: Money management per account (owner 2026-09-18). STRATEGY lives in
code and is the SAME for every account - only what is listed here may
differ. Change a number, and the bots pick it up within a minute; no
restart, no code edit.
'extends' inherits every field of another package, so a new offer is
usually two lines. Add an account to 'accounts' to put it on a package;
an account that is not listed gets 'base'.
RESTART REQUIRED. The loader re-reads this file every 60 s, but a bot
resolves its package ONCE at import and keeps the values as module
constants - so nothing here reaches a RUNNING bot. Change a dial, then
restart that account's structure_bos_bot.py. (Corrected 2026-09-20; the
old note here claimed no restart was needed, which was never true.)
day_cap        stop opening once today's REALISED profit reaches this
(waived while the account owes money). null = no cap.
max_trades_day how many trades a day this package allows. null = no cap.
week_target    shown at startup, informational only.
base_lot       lot per signal.  max_extra: recovery bullets on top.
kill_net       close everything and stop at this net loss.
max_risk_pct   no single trade may risk more than this share of balance.
debt_mode      'hwm' = debt is the drawdown from the peak.
'half' = half of each loss is added to the debt.

nervosity  false = this account ignores the 1.00x nervosity brake. OFF EVERYWHERE since 2026-09-22 by owner decision: it helped on only 5 of 12 anchors, its halves disagreed, its sign flipped with spread and it cost HALF the volume (review/nerv_gate_test.py). The >= 1.85x exception is NOT this dial - it lives in code and no account can switch it off.

movement   false = this account ignores the movement brake too (no big move in 2 h / no small move in 1 h). Owner 2026-09-21: kept TRUE everywhere after review/move_gate_test.py - it never lost on any cut and costs ~4% of volume, unlike nervosity.
NEITHER dial can switch off the >= 1.85x 'tres agite' exception. That is a floor in code (NERV_STORM), not a setting.
day_cap_waived  true (default, EVERY account, since 2026-09-24) = the
day_cap is WAIVED while the account owes money, so it
keeps taking full trades (not just recovery bullets)
until the debt clears, then the cap binds again. false
= the cap ALWAYS stops the account at target, debt or
not. Owner 2026-09-23 measured false winning for 441 at
a $10 cap - but that test (cap_waiver_test.py) never
modelled the midpoint bullets that ACTUALLY run during
debt. Redone 2026-09-24 with bullets included: true
(today's default) wins at every cap tested, $3/$5/$10,
by $10-$39 (review/day_cap_always_binds_test.py) - the
full-size trades waiving unlocks are worth more than
the bullets alone. 441 moved back to true the same day.
nervosity, movement and day_cap_waived are the ONLY strategy dials allowed in this
file, and both exist for the same reason: neither brake has ever been
shown to make money, so switching them off is a control arm, not a new
strategy. Everything else about the structure rules stays in code and
is identical on every account.
scale_with_balance  true = base_lot and day_cap are recomputed ONCE PER
UTC DAY from the account's own balance that morning:
lot = base_lot * (balance/scale_ref_balance), floored
at 0.01; day_cap scales the same way. Owner
2026-09-23: 'Valere is a good example... can we make
a formula such that lots update progressively with
balance?' - Valere's $3/day on $200 IS the reference
ratio, so every account (Dad's $10 target included,
by owner decision) now scales off the same $200
anchor instead of staying frozen at whatever the
balance was when the package was written.
scale_ref_balance   the balance at which base_lot/day_cap are exactly
the numbers written below. 200.0 = Valere's own
balance when the $3/day ratio was set.
